editorial:
Imagine sitting in your own living room when suddenly, a voice starts coming through your smart speakers. It is not a podcast or a song, but a recording of a real murder happening in real time. That is exactly what happens to Kate, and it sets off a wild ride of panic and confusion. You will feel the tension as she tries to figure out if someone is playing a mean joke on her or if a killer is actually nearby. The vibe is very creepy because it uses technology that you probably have in your own house, making the whole thing feel way too close to home.

The acting is solid and the pacing keeps you on the edge of your seat without feeling too rushed. While some of the plot twists are a bit predictable, the suspense makes up for it. You should definitely check this out if you love mysteries that keep you guessing.
endingExplained: The big twist is that the audio was not a recording from the past, but a live feed from the house next door. Kate discovers that her neighbor is the killer and has been hacking her home system to taunt her. In the final scenes, Kate uses her own smart devices to trap the killer and alert the police. It ends with the killer getting arrested and Kate finally feeling safe in her home again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves high-tech mysteries and suspenseful home-invasion stories.
